issues: 0-2s: Caption states 'Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores on the two sister chromatids' (implying bi-/amphitelic orientation), but the duplicated chromosome is drawn clearly LEFT of the metaphase plate and the right-pole microtubule does not visibly reach or bind the right kinetochore. The initial geometry contradicts the stated fully-attached state.
3-11s: 'moves toward the middle' is acceptable for congression, but it follows the contradictory 0-2s frame, so the alignment narrative starts from an inconsistent unattached/off-center state.
12-23s: Sister separation (anaphase) with each chromatid pulled to its own pole is directionally correct and consistent with prior bi-orientation once centered.
3-7s: Label ghosting/double-rendering — 'Copy B'/'Copy A' appear as 'CopyBB'/'CopyAA' and 'Microtubule' text is doubled/overlapping, reducing legibility.
0-2s: Right microtubule terminates near the metaphase plate rather than at the right kinetochore, making the attachment ambiguous/inconsistent with the caption.
8-11s: Chromosome correctly centered on the metaphase plate with both kinetochores bound; this portion is visually consistent.

pedagogy.accuracy: REVISE — initial attachment claim (0-2s) not supported by the drawn geometry; later stages (centering, then poleward separation) are accurate.
pedagogy.terms: PASS — 'sister chromatids', 'kinetochores', 'microtubules/spindle fibers', 'metaphase plate', 'pole' used correctly; 'Copy A/B' is a non-standard but acceptable teaching label for the two sisters.
pedagogy.motion: PASS — congression to the plate (3-11s) then symmetric poleward movement of separated sisters (12-23s) is shown with clear direction over time.
pedagogy.density: PASS — appropriately low for high school; one duplicated chromosome keeps focus.
pedagogy.readability: REVISE — text ghosting at 3-7s and the off-center initial chromosome hurt clarity.
pedagogy.objective: PASS — clearly aims to show metaphase alignment followed by anaphase separation, and largely achieves it.

limitations: Schematic 2D representation: no depiction of cohesin cleavage, kinetochore–microtubule dynamic instability, or spindle checkpoint that drive real attachment/separation.
Only one chromosome shown; does not convey genome-wide coordination or the metaphase-to-anaphase transition trigger.
Frame sampling is sparse; exact moment of right-kinetochore attachment and the onset of separation (around 11-12s) cannot be precisely verified between sampled frames.
No scale, time axis, or cell boundary, so 'middle of the cell' is only implied by the metaphase plate line.
